import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 31

The WOWII page records this as **Chung's theorem**: proved in F. R. K. Chung,
*The average distance and the independence number*, J. Graph Theory **12** (1988),
229-235. We state it here as a theorem; the formal proof is left as `sorry`
pending a Lean port of Chung's argument.

Here $\mathrm{path}(G)$ is the floor of the average distance over ordered pairs
of distinct vertices (definition `path` in `FormalConjecturesForMathlib`), and
$\mathrm{rad}(G)$ is the graph radius.

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture31

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 31](http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj31)
(Chung 1988):

For every simple connected graph $G$,
$\mathrm{path}(G) \ge 2 \cdot \mathrm{rad}(G) - 1$,
where $\mathrm{path}(G)$ is the floor of the average distance and
$\mathrm{rad}(G)$ is the graph radius.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture31 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected) :
    2 * (G.radius.toNat : ℤ) - 1 ≤ (path G : ℤ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The `path G` invariant cast to ℤ is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ (path G : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _

/-- The radius cast to ℤ is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ (G.radius.toNat : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture31

findings.description: The theorem docstring, repeated in the module docstring, describes `path G` as the floor of average distance. The imported `SimpleGraph.path` instead counts vertices in a largest induced path, which is the correct invariant for WOWII 31. These definitions genuinely differ: independent Lean proofs establish `path K₂ = 2` and `averageDistance K₂ = 1`. The formal statement is correct; the prose is stale.
findings.source_evidence: WOWII Conjecture 31 states `path(G) ≥ 2rad(G) − 1`. Its definition 35 explicitly defines path(G) as “The number of vertices of a largest induced path of the graph.” Definition script read at http://web.archive.org/web/20240726225301id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowii/wowIIdefs.js .
findings.suggested_fix: In both docstrings, replace the floor-of-average-distance description with “the number of vertices in a largest induced path.” Leave the Lean inequality and imported definition unchanged.

findings.description: The module attributes the proof to Chung’s 1988 paper, The average distance and the independence number, and the theorem docstring repeats “Chung 1988.” That paper proves the independence-number/average-distance inequality, not the induced-path/radius theorem stated here. WOWII’s reference instead points to Erdős–Saks–Sós (1986), whose Theorem 2.2 gives the required inequality and credits its proof to Fan Chung.
findings.source_evidence: WOWII’s reference button for Conjecture 31 invokes `printConjRef(30)`, pointing to Maximum Induced Trees in Graphs. In that paper, Theorem 2.2 and its proof occur on pp. 64–65, with the explicit statement: “The following proof of Theorem 2.2 was provided by Fan Chung, replacing a cumbersome proof given in a previous version of the paper.” See https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1986-08.pdf . Chung’s cited 1988 paper, read in full at https://fanchung.ucsd.edu/mypaps/fanpap/99_avgdist.pdf , proves that independence number is at least average distance.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the 1988 citation with P. Erdős, M. Saks and V. T. Sós, Maximum Induced Trees in Graphs, Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B 41 (1986), 61–79, Theorem 2.2, noting that the proof is due to Fan Chung. Update the theorem docstring’s parenthetical attribution accordingly. Retain `category research solved`.

reformulations.difference: Lean requires `[Nontrivial α]`, while the source states the result for every connected graph without that restriction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A connected graph has a nonempty vertex type. If that type is not nontrivial, it is a singleton and its radius is zero, so the omitted inequality is simply `−1 ≤ (path G : ℤ)`, which holds by nonnegativity. Thus the universally quantified statement with the nontriviality restriction is equivalent to the unrestricted finite connected-graph statement. The equivalence, including the adjacency-decidability parameter, was proved independently in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`.

sources_consulted: WOWII Conjecture 31 and adjacent remarks: http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj31 , read through http://web.archive.org/web/20260723161800id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html .
WOWII definitions 13, 21 and 35, and the Conjecture 31 reference: http://web.archive.org/web/20240726225301id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowii/wowIIdefs.js .
P. Erdős, M. Saks and V. T. Sós, Maximum Induced Trees in Graphs, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 41 (1986), 61–79; definitions and Theorem 2.2 with its proof: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1986-08.pdf .

F. R. K. Chung, The average distance and the independence number, J. Graph Theory 12 (1988), 229–235; all seven pages, using OCR of the scanned paper: https://fanchung.ucsd.edu/mypaps/fanpap/99_avgdist.pdf .
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the Lean statements. Both sanity-check examples are correct, and WOWII records the result as a known theorem. Checked the maximum-over-induced-paths definition, empty and singleton cases, and that connected finite graphs have finite radius, so `radius.toNat` cannot use its infinity default. The scratch proofs and small-graph computations compile successfully; they do not use `conjecture31`.
